open_points.subject: M22 SpooledFile write ownership
open_points.text: "Two have several, on purpose: StoredValue M21 ...; NodeExecution M23 ..."
open_points.question: If only those two record types are intentionally multi-writer, which module owns creating SpooledFile (M22) records and setting their semantic fields (especially disclosure_class) for function outputs versus operation outputs?
options: store is the sole owner of M22 creation and metadata
runs owns function-produced M22 and effects owns operation-produced M22
service_invoker owns operation-produced M22 while runs owns function-produced M22
open_points.default_guess: runs writes function-produced spool metadata, effects writes operation-produced spool metadata, both via store.spool_file

open_points.subject: Repair view record set for a slot
open_points.text: A15 rule 6: "the latest NodeExecutions ... of function nodes pinned to any contract version of that slot" vs State 3: "surface ... pages the NodeExecutions whose executed implementation is in that set"
open_points.question: Must the repair view include function-node NodeExecutions with status skipped_by_guard or upstream_failed (where executed is absent), or only records that name an executed implementation?
options: include all function-node NodeExecutions for the slot's contract versions, including non-executed statuses
include only NodeExecutions that name an executed implementation
open_points.default_guess: include only records with executed implementation IDs (as written in State 3)

open_points.subject: Source of instance facts at send time
open_points.text: "bindings.check_binding_current returns ... api_base_url, required_headers and class of the instance ..." and then "service_invoker.prepare_request ... owns every instance failure — no selected instance, no api_base_url, a repeated required header"
open_points.question: At send time, does service_invoker validate instance facts only from data returned by bindings, or may/should it re-read installation state itself for selected instance details?
options: bindings is the sole reader of selected-instance manifest data; service_invoker validates only what bindings passes
service_invoker re-reads installation/manifest instance data itself and bindings returns only capability-level facts
both may read instance data independently
open_points.default_guess: bindings passes raw instance facts (possibly missing), service_invoker performs the send-time instance validations on those facts
